en.name: Kizito
en.summary: Youngest of the Uganda Martyrs, a royal page only about thirteen years old when he was burned alive for his Christian faith.
en.body: Kizito served as one of the young pages in the royal court of King Mwanga II of Buganda, in present-day Uganda, the youngest of the group of Catholic converts among the pages who, under the instruction and example of their leader Charles Lwanga, resisted the king's demands for sexual relations and embraced Christian teaching despite the danger this posed under Mwanga's increasingly hostile rule. Reportedly known among his companions for a lively, mischievous personality alongside his sincere faith, he was among those baptized secretly by Lwanga the night before the mass execution of the Christian pages was carried out in 1886, and he was burned alive at Namugongo along with his companions, said to have remained calm and even joked with his fellow martyrs as they awaited death. His youth made him a particularly poignant figure among the twenty-two Catholic martyrs of Uganda, and he was canonized together with them by Pope Paul VI in 1964, the first canonized saints of modern sub-Saharan Africa.
